checks.label: Factorising is the reverse process to expanding brackets: on every screen the bracket expands back to the expression it started from, making the same value at every number tried, whole, a half or negative

The greatest common factor is the largest that divides evenly into all the terms: every answer takes out the largest whole number dividing every term, so what is left inside shares nothing more (12x and 18 share 2, 3 and 6, the biggest 6)

The factor outside of the parentheses is multiplied by each term inside: each puzzle accepts only the answer that multiplies back to the start, and every wrong answer offered either makes a different value at the number tried or, true but not finished, still has a factor shared inside its bracket

Expanding brackets does not change the value of an expression, as it is two ways of writing the same one: on the first screen 6x + 15 and 3(2x + 5) both make 27 at x = 2, and the same as each other wherever x is slid from 1 to 6, the rectangle staying 3 rows of 2x + 5

R = R₀(1 + αΔT) gives the resistance R after a temperature change ΔT, where R₀ is the original resistance: R₀ + R₀αΔT factorises back to it, and for the example winding of 2.0 Ω cold and 2.4 Ω after a run, 2.0 + 0.4 = 2.0 × 1.2, drawn as a block R₀ tall, R₀ × 1, and the strip R₀αΔT

V = IR₁ + IR₂ + IR₃ = I(R₁ + R₂ + R₃): with the example 2 A through 3, 5 and 2 Ω the three parts make 6 + 10 + 4 = 20 V and I(R₁ + R₂ + R₃) makes 2 × 10 = 20 V, drawn as I rows of R₁ + R₂ + R₃ squares, each worth 1 V

Every worked number is right (27 at x = 2; 28, 88 and 30; 30 at x = 1; 20, 20 and 56; 2.4 Ω and 1.2; 20, 15 and 40 at x = 3; 20 V; 24, 60 and 12; 9, 9 and 39 at x = 4; 7, 49 and −119; 8, 6 and 10; 20, 20 and 44), and every line of working on every screen adds up

Every rectangle is drawn to count: once fitted it holds the factor's rows of bars and squares, each bar x long and each square 1, filling exactly the height and length its sides name, with a split line where each part ends; before a puzzle is answered the same pieces lie loose inside the drawing
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture shows the answer: the parts lie loose, with no height, no bracket, no split line and no answer row
Trying the number: a right answer makes the same value as the question; a wrong one shows in red making a different value, or, true but not finished, shows in red what its bracket still shares
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
